cells.tense: The beginning is here and your hands are steady for it.
cells.act: share your strength where it is needed
cells.ask: Pick someone you're close to and offer them one concrete piece of what you're good at this week. Name the day you'll do it, keep it that size, and finish it.
cells.core:
When someone you're close to is carrying something heavy, you can stand beside them and give real weight to it without becoming the whole load. You feel with them and stay your own size. What you hand over goes where it's needed, and neither of you has to keep a count.

The seed of that is live right now. Give it one small place to land: someone you're close to gets one concrete piece of what you're good at, once this week. Pick the day, keep it that size, finish it. You'll find out what you actually hold when you set part of it down in someone's hands, and they get something with weight behind it. Nothing about their response has to come back to you for it to count.
cells.sheetLine: You can feel with someone and still hand them something real.
cells.verb: Starting something real and small in a shared life
cells.place: In how close you can stand to another person

cells.tense: You are already building for people what they haven't asked for yet.
cells.act: know the feeling fully before you move on
cells.ask: With someone close, name what you actually felt before you did anything about it. Say it plainly, even if only to yourself.
cells.core:
With the people closest to you, the next move gets made before the feeling is full. You know what's needed, or you think you do, and the fixing starts early. To them it's help that arrived already decided, and the half-formed things get held back from you now.

What's underneath is that you want them close. But a feeling has to be finished before you can hold anything for someone else — half-felt, it becomes your own push, and push reads as force from the other chair. So next time, before the hands move, name what you felt. You'll find out whether the moment wanted your work or only your attention, and you'll know which by how light they seem afterward.

cells.tense: The moment to start was there and you keep standing past it.
cells.act: see it whole, with nothing hidden
cells.ask: Look at a shared moment that already happened, all of it, without adding anything to it or taking anything away.
cells.core:
With the people close to you, the real moment is usually behind you before you arrive in it. You check in after, apologise after, mean it after. Standing near someone, the question of what they're actually feeling doesn't get asked, so the closeness stays in the planning and doesn't reach the hour.

Nothing here needs pushing. Seeing goes a long way, so try it whole first. Pick a shared moment that already happened, one of the flat ones, and look at all of it — what you said, what they did, what the room was like. Add nothing, take nothing out. You aren't repairing it or promising anything. Just let the whole of it be visible once. The connection is still there to be met, and it isn't waiting on you to feel more.

cells.tense: The warmth between people is being made, and you're the one making it.
cells.act: lay every piece of it out where you can see all of it at once
cells.ask: Lay out on paper every small thing you do to keep a close relationship warm. Just the list, no grades in the margin.
cells.core:
In your close relationships, the bridge is up because you are quietly one end of it. You ask the second question. You remember what matters to them. You keep the tone warm when the room goes flat, and it works — people come to you and leave lighter.

Ask you about it and it's just what a person does. But the closeness you feel is partly your own work, and the work has been done from behind rather than from the front. So lay out on paper every small thing you do to keep one close relationship warm — the list, not the story. No grades in the margin. Seeing it flat on one page is the whole thing: it stops being something the room gives you and goes back into your own hands.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that the person is avoiding or withholding in the Too Little cell — the record only says the capacity is under-expressed and past-anchored, not why or what happened. A reader could reasonably say the shrinking came from exhaustion or circumstances rather than hesitation, so the ask (seeing one shared situation whole for exactly one minute and not repairing anything) is still useful either way because it demands no feeling and no effort in the starved seat. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is 'the moment has already passed' — it sounds like a verdict, so the Too Little core locates the standing without saying what kept them there. Both Too Much and Too Little are the two directions the same seed goes wrong — one thrown forward onto people, one never left in the hand — so the two cores must mirror each other. All four acts are verbatim from the Support and Clarity lists; each ask takes a different verb (offer, sit, see, lay).
